protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; one owner-recording entry for DR-003 scoped preview TM under adopted D-054 / D-057

notesRecorded.location: Authority and dependency pins — 'Route B selection D-030 commit d5721222623faa854d85282df408de1c5005d19f'
notesRecorded.observation: The pin is true: a git log -S search for the '## D-030 —' heading against COORD returns d572122 as the commit that introduced it. But that commit's subject line reads 'D-035: record doctor-contract.v4 as DR-114 design contract', so a reader who verifies the pin the obvious way — git log -1 on the hash — sees a subject naming a different decision and can reasonably conclude the pin is false.
notesRecorded.whyItIsNotAFinding: Nothing is inaccurate. The commit genuinely carries D-030's adoption, and D-057 clause 3 requires the pin, not a particular phrasing of it.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecording: The sibling D-060 entry pins the same commit for D-028 and writes 'first COORD appearance commit d5721222…'. Those three words convert a pin that looks wrong on casual inspection into one that states its own verification method. I nearly filed this exact axis as a blocker on an earlier draft by reading the commit subject instead of its contents, and this dispatch lists it as an attack axis, so the trap is live. The fix costs three words and the wording already exists in the family.

notesRecorded.location: Decision clause 1 — 'As the named file-08 owner under D-054'
notesRecorded.observation: DR-003 is the only row in this family whose file-08 owner is a pair that includes the coordinator itself: 'Threat-model authority + V1 coordinator'. The pinned disposition carries a caveat aimed precisely at that: 'Coordinator may draft. D-000 does not make the coordinator Threat-model authority. File 08 names V1 coordinator as co-owner: the coordinator may record jointly; it does not replace that authority.' Clause 1 says 'owner' in the singular and the entry does not carry that caveat anywhere in its own text.
notesRecorded.whyItIsNotAFinding: I tested the authority rather than the phrasing. D-054 names the owner roles it reaches explicitly — 'the named V1 owners (Evidence, TM, D9, retention, R-1, identity surfaces)' — and TM is in that list. So the grant supplies the Threat-model half, D-000 supplies the coordinator half, and the assistant holds both; the joint recording the caveat demands is satisfied rather than bypassed. The entry also pins the owner role verbatim as 'Threat-model authority + V1 coordinator', which matches file 08's DR-003 owner cell as an exact string, and pins the disposition by digest so the caveat is incorporated. Nothing is false and nothing is unauthorized.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecording: This is the one row where the gap between 'owner' and 'owners' could have mattered, because the coordinator drafting the entry is one of the two co-owners and the source document specifically warns against the coordinator standing in for the other authority. The entry is saved by D-054's owner list, not by anything it says itself. A clause reading 'as the named file-08 owners — Threat-model authority and V1 coordinator, the TM role exercised under D-054's owner list' would make the entry self-supporting instead of leaving the reader to reconstruct why the coordinator may record on the TM row. Compare D-060, which uses the plural for its multi-authority row.

summary: Subject and prompt both locked at 0444 and both held at their dispatched digests. The distinctive risk on DR-003 is the security-complete claim, and the entry blocks it explicitly in the operative clause — 'Not a security-complete claim. TM stays UNSET for the freeze' — which is faithful to the disposition's own honesty field and confirmed against the freeze, where TM carries 'UNSET — BLOCKS FREEZE'. All six digests match live bytes, all four commits resolve, the Route A remainder is an exact three-item match against the disposition's own field, and the owner role is an exact string match against file 08's DR-003 cell. My two notes are clarity, not defect: a commit pin that is true but reader-hostile, and a singular 'owner' on the one row where the coordinator is a co-owner.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 4c9495c0be14e22742e4337d808dc4a7839362506431acf1b68f702193f9de57, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest. Prompt held at 31bc149b3ebc514e4f7f54f7019bbad2f81db3094a2fefa5bf8a57c01a58c767. Both files -r--r--r-- at both ends. This is the second dispatch in the family to lock both.

The attack 'security-complete claim' fails, and this is the axis that matters most on DR-003. Clause 2 reads 'This may discharge condition 1 for DR-003 within architecture-preview scope only. Not a security-complete claim. TM stays UNSET for the freeze.' I checked both halves against sources rather than accepting them. The disposition's honesty field says 'Preview may be designed against this scoped TM. That is not a security-complete claim. File 08's blueprint-impact cell (No V2 blueprint or security-complete claim) remains true for any claim wider than the architecture preview', and its condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded adds 'It does not authorize a security-complete claim.' The freeze independently confirms the second half: TM carries 'UNSET — BLOCKS FREEZE' in §3.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails. The header states 'Does not mark SATISFIED', clause 3 states 'Does not mark DR-003 SATISFIED. The Route A remainder above stays owed. Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization', and the readiness effect states 'Zero SATISFIED. Conditions 2–5 unchanged.' That tracks the disposition's condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded, which says conditions 2-5 remain independently required and condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization.

The attack 'missing D-054 / D-057 / D-030 pins' fails. All three are present: D-054 by path, sha256 and commit 29670ed…; D-057 by commit 33597e8…; D-030 as the Route B selection by commit d5721222…. The dependency declaration names the same three and states that revocation requires this owner's supersession and reconciliation of dependent MF-6 notes. D-041 is additionally pinned as the coordinator recording.

The attack 'missing verdict paths' fails. Both are pinned by path and sha256, both recited as ACCEPT 0/0. I opened my own — route-b.DR-003.preview-tm.v2.review-independent.claude2.json — and confirmed verdict ACCEPT with 0 blockers and 0 advisories, so the recital of my verdict is accurate and 'Operative riders: none' is correct on my side. I additionally checked adopted D-041 for any DR-003 rider and found none: zero hits for advisory, rider, RB-DR003, or operative.

The attack 'incomplete Route A remainder' fails, tested by string equality against the disposition's whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA: three items each, exact match, same order — reviewed closure of V10/custody and G19; publication block satisfied by required demonstration; final TM disposition for the authoritative product.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails. All six verify: COORD 540587a4…, file 08 6547e6ac…, the D-054 amendment, the DR-003 preview-tm v2 disposition, and both v2 verdicts. The COORD pin is a different value from the one D-060 cites, and 540587a4… is the current live digest, so this entry re-measured rather than copying its sibling's stale pin.

The attack 'condition 5 / file 08' fails. The header refuses to edit file 08 or authorize docs/v2/implementation/, clause 3 preserves condition 5 as the only implementation authorization, clause 4 refuses the file 08 edit under MF-6 and defers a cell note as a separate act, file 08 measures unchanged at its pinned digest, and git reports zero modified tracked files.

All four cited commits resolve at full hash and the two first-appearance claims check out by contents: 29670ed 'D-054: user amendment for preview-scope owner recording', 33597e8 'D-057: mechanics for preview-scope owner recording', d572122 introducing the '## D-030 —' heading, and 56973db 'D-040/D-041: record accepted Route B drafts for DR-008 and DR-003', which is also the commit that introduced the '## D-041 —' heading and which names DR-003 in its own subject.

The owner role is an exact string match: file 08's DR-003 owner cell reads 'Threat-model authority + V1 coordinator' and the entry pins the identical string. The disposition's ownerWhoMustRecord names the same pair.

The register standing supports every dependency: D-030, D-041, D-054 and D-057 are all present, ADOPTED, and not CONTESTED. D-060, whose cycle I reviewed immediately before this one, is now adopted, which is consistent with COORD having moved to a new digest.

Scope discipline holds. The header and clause 5 both state the entry does not owner-record DR-002, DR-004, DR-005, or DR-008, and the protocol line states 'One owner-recording entry. Own commit.' The disposition's own scope field, 'architecture preview (D-002 / D-018) only', matches the entry's scope pin.

Reversibility is the correct compound form and does not reach back into its authorities: 'Compound. Overturn: C-D065, plus reconciliation of any later MF-6 note. Does not overturn D-030, D-041, D-054, or D-057.'
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Its file exists and I hashed it at b4c8e1064870f31025683aacea816dc7c60983c8eddd7e73729a97d834825b78 without opening it.

The merits of the DR-003 preview-tm v2 disposition beyond my separate ACCEPT review of it, whose stated limits I carry forward.
Whether the earlier five-entry D-059-063 draft, which covered overlapping rows, is withdrawn. Still unstated across files.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. DR-003 is the row where a preview recording could quietly read as a security claim, and the entry refuses that in its operative clause with language faithful to the disposition's own honesty field, backed by the freeze still carrying TM as UNSET — BLOCKS FREEZE. Both notes are clarity rather than defect, and I want the reasoning on the second one visible: I did not accept the singular 'owner' on a co-owned row, I went to D-054 and found TM named in its owner list, which is what makes the recording authorized. The entry is correct; it just leaves that step for the reader to reconstruct.
